newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK WIDENS CROWN FLUCTUATION BANDS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK WIDENS CROWN FLUCTUATION BANDS.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Thursday it would widen the fluctuation bands within which the crown is fixed against its mark/dollar basket to plus/minus seven percent from plus minus five percent on January 1 1997.

"In our monetary programme for 1997 we decided to widen the fluctuation band for fixing the crown to bring more uncertainty for the inflow of short-term, speculative capital," said Vladimir Masar, the governor of the NBS.
Masar he said he expected that the move would be sufficient to achieve the central bank's aims.
The NBS governor also warned that the band would be used to its full extent in 1997.
"We will use the fluctuation band in its entire range more significantly than we did in 1996, according to the market situation," said Masar.
Masar said the move would to some extent counteract the wide interest rate differential between Slovakia and western countries.
Interest rates on the Slovak interbank money market range between 12.4 percent and 14.2 percent.
